data.title: A Rag GTPase dimer code defines the regulation of mTORC1 by amino acids
data.authors: Gollwitzer P; Grützmacher N; Wilhelm S; Kümmel D; Demetriades C

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Human cells (genetically modified Rag-paralogue cell lines)
data.finding: The four mammalian Rag GTPase paralogues are not functionally interchangeable: RagC/D determines substrate specificity (RagD favors TFEB/TFE3 phosphorylation via tighter LAMTOR binding), while RagA/B determines the response to amino acid withdrawal (RagB-expressing cells keep mTORC1 lysosomal and active even upon starvation). Author correction issued 2023 (PMID 36536178, no change to conclusions).
data.abstract_excerpt: Amino acid availability controls mTORC1 activity via a heterodimeric Rag GTPase complex that functions as a scaffold at the lysosomal surface, bringing together mTORC1 with its activators and effectors. Mammalian cells express four Rag proteins (RagA-D) that form dimers composed of RagA/B bound to RagC/D. Traditionally, the Rag paralogue pairs (RagA/B and RagC/D) are referred to as functionally redundant, with the four dimer combinations used interchangeably in most studies.

extracted_findings.intervention: Cell lines engineered to express single Rag heterodimers; amino-acid withdrawal
extracted_findings.target: Rag GTPase paralogues (RagA/B, RagC/D), mTORC1 substrate selection, TFEB/TFE3
extracted_findings.effect: RagD promotes phosphorylation of lysosomal substrates TFEB/TFE3 through tighter LAMTOR binding, while RagB-expressing cells keep mTORC1 lysosomal and active even during starvation.
